To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presence of carotid bruit is an important risk factor for atherosclerotic vascular disease and that carotid bruits are associated with an increased risk of myocardial infarction.

the presence of a carotid bruit is a risk factor for atherosclerosis and is associated with a 3-fold increase in the risk of stroke, and that the presence or absence, and laterality, of the bruit is not sufficient to reliably indicate the presence or absence or the degree of aortic atherosclerosis in a given individual patient.
the presence of a carotid bruit is associated with an increased risk of coronary artery disease, peripheral arterial disease, and stroke.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new noninvasive method of detecting and quantitating atherosclerotic plaque in the carotid arteries.
the study of the mechanisms underlying the pathophysiology of the carotid bruit and its association with the development of stroke and other cardiovascular diseases.
the development of an integrated approach for the diagnosis of cardiovascular disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
carotid bruit, as a marker of carotid artery atherosclerosis, is a risk factor for coronary heart disease, stroke, and death from all causes.
carotid bruits are associated with increased risk of systemic vascular disease.
carotid bruits are associated with an increased risk of carotid artery disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bruits are a sign of increased risk for cardiovascular disease.

the presence of bruit in a patient with risk factors for atherosclerosis should alert the physician to the possibility of atherosclerotic disease in the neck, but that the presence of a neck bruit does not predict the severity of aortic atheroma in a patient with aortic stenosis or the severity of carotid disease in patients with stroke.
the presence of a carotid bruit should be considered a marker of increased cardiovascular risk, and that the absence of a bruit is not sufficient to exclude a high risk of atherosclerosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the carotid bruit is not a good indicator of carotid artery disease, but it is a good predictor of coronary artery disease.
carotid artery stenosis is a risk factor for ischemic stroke, and that the risk is higher with more severe stenosis and higher with symptomatic than with asymptomatic disease.
the presence of a carotid bruit is a marker of increased risk of systemic disease, but it is not a reliable marker for the presence of atherosclerosis at a specific level in a given patient.
